story_type: soldiers join wildland fire crews cutting a fire break in a burning forest
hook: Soldiers trained for war walked into a burning forest.
narration: These soldiers trained for war. That day, they walked into a burning forest.
It was August 2015, and wildfires were tearing through northeast Washington.
Soldiers from Joint Base Lewis McChord joined fire crews from Oregon and North Dakota.
First they ran hose lines down the trail and coupled the sections together.
Then came the fire break: a strip of ground stripped of anything that can burn, so the flames run out of fuel when they reach it.
The crews cut away brush and dragged downed branches out of the fire's path.
outcome: The soldiers laid out fire hose and cleared a fire break alongside the fire crews.
title: Soldiers cut a fire break in a burning forest
description:
Soldiers from Task Force First Round out of Joint Base Lewis-McChord helped firefighters from Oregon and North Dakota fight wildfires in northeast Washington in August 2015, laying out fire hose and clearing vegetation for a fire break.

Footage: U.S. Army video by Sgt. Chad Guthrie, 28th Public Affairs Detachment, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/420830/soldiers-help-suppress-wildfire
